### Day 281: Acts 22:1–21
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-281-acts-22-121.html
Passage: Acts 22:1-21
Points:
- Paul communicated clearly and connected with his hearers by avoiding confusing insider jargon.
- He shared his former sinful conduct with humility, relating to the audience without superiority.
- He kept the focus on the Savior rather than glorifying ungodly past behavior.
- He showed that every Christian testimony matters regardless of whether the conversion was dramatic.
- He explained God's calling to demonstrate that salvation gives believers an active earthly purpose.

### Devotional: Acts 22
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/genesis-23-matthew-22-nehemiah-12-acts-22/
Passage: Acts 22:1-21
Points:
- The Jerusalem crowd listened patiently until Paul stated Christ sent him to the Gentiles.
- The mob reacted violently because their religious and cultural identity felt threatened.
- The audience treated God as their exclusive tribal possession rather than Lord of the nations.
- Modern Christians can make the same mistake by domesticating Scripture to fit their culture.
- Paul appealed to his Roman citizenship to establish legal protections for other believers.
